chief_complaint: new lump in the right breast
hpi_details: 55F presents after feeling a painless, hard, fixed lump in her right breast during a self-exam. She has no nipple discharge or skin changes but noticed a palpable lymph node in her right axilla.

core_concepts: A painless, hard, fixed breast mass in an older woman is cancer until proven otherwise.
common_misconceptions: Assuming pain implies cancer (breast cancer is typically painless initially).
dangerous_errors: Reassuring without triple assessment (exam, imaging, biopsy).
management_principles: Bilateral diagnostic mammogram, targeted ultrasound, and core needle biopsy.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: SAGES & ACS Evidence-Based Surgical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 55F with a new painless hard right breast mass and axillary lump.
reference_soap.objective: 2cm hard, non-mobile mass in right upper outer quadrant. 1cm firm right axillary lymph node.
reference_soap.plan: Diagnostic mammogram and ultrasound, refer for core needle biopsy.

learning_objectives: Initiate the proper workup (triple assessment) for a suspicious breast mass.

teaching.one_liner: A painless, hard, fixed breast mass with axillary lymphadenopathy in a postmenopausal woman requiring urgent triple assessment.

must_ask.say: Is the lump hard, and does it feel like it moves freely or is it fixed in place?
When did you first notice the lump, and has it changed in size?
Have you noticed any dimpling of the skin, nipple discharge, or nipple pulling inward?
Have you felt any lumps under your arm?
Does anyone in your family have a history of breast or ovarian cancer?

history.answer: I found a new lump in my right breast about a week ago during a self-exam, and I also felt a small bump in my right armpit.
I first felt it about a week ago while checking my breasts in the shower.
It is in the upper outer area of my right breast, feels about the size of a small walnut, and is only on the right side.
Since I discovered it last week, it has stayed about the same size and hasn't gone away.
I went through menopause five years ago, so I no longer have monthly menstrual cycles.
No, it does not hurt at all, even when I press right on it.
No, I haven't noticed any skin dimpling, orange-peel texture, redness, or nipple retraction.
No, there has been no discharge, fluid, or bleeding from either nipple.
Yes, while feeling around after finding the breast lump, I found a firm, pea-sized knot in my right armpit.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or local heat or redness in the breast.
I have never been pregnant and have never breastfed.
No, I haven't lost weight, and I have no bone pain, chronic cough, or trouble breathing.
No, I haven't had any trauma to my chest, and I've never had any cosmetic breast procedures.
I have never had any breast lumps, cysts, biopsies, or radiation to my chest.
My last routine screening mammogram was two years ago, and they said everything looked completely clear.
No one in my family has had breast, ovarian, or any other cancer that I know of.
I had my first period at age twelve and reached menopause at age fifty.
I have been taking postmenopausal hormone replacement therapy for the past five years for hot flashes.
Other than the hormone replacement therapy, I just take a daily multivitamin.
I am very worried that this hard lump could be breast cancer.
I am terrified that if it is cancer, I might have to lose my breast to a mastectomy.
I would like to get a mammogram and ultrasound done today, and find out if I need a biopsy.
I don't have any chronic medical illnesses like high blood pressure or diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I do not have any allergies to medications, food, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only drink an occasional glass of wine on special occasions.
I work as an office administrative assistant and live with my husband.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 122/76 mmHg, pulse 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.

A 2 cm hard, non-mobile, non-tender mass in the right upper outer quadrant, no skin dimpling or nipple retraction, no nipple discharge bilaterally, and a 1 cm firm, non-tender right axillary lymph node.
No palpable cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy on either side.
Symmetrical chest wall with normal expansion, and the breast mass does not fix to the underlying chest wall muscle.
Clear breath sounds throughout both lung fields with no crackles or wheezes.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal first and second heart sounds and no murmurs.
No erythema, skin thickening, peau d'orange, or rash on the chest or breast skin.
